definitions: To make someone feel less confident or enthusiastic by saying or doing something unexpected.
To pre-empt someone's argument or plan, thereby diminishing its impact or effectiveness.
examples: Her sudden resignation really took the wind out of his sails.
The rival company's announcement took the wind out of their sails just before their product launch.
He thought he had a great idea, but her earlier comment took the wind out of his sails.
lemma: to take the wind out of one's sails
synonyms: to pull the rug out from under someone
source: to take the wind out of one's sails
